link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.question: The nine existing chains' link 2b is a CODEGEN flip. What is it for a CTFE flip?
link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.seam: mir_for_ctfe (trust_ir_flip.rs:194, try_flip_ctfe), gated on hir_body_const_context being Const or Static -- a const FN is NOT a candidate here, it belongs to the codegen seam
link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.what_it_binds: the VALUE. The const-eval interpreter evaluated MIR re-derived from THIS trust-ir module, and the constant every use site of META_TAG is given is that evaluation's output.
link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.what_it_does_NOT_bind: no machine code corresponds to these nine instructions. The comparison, the assert and the shift all ran at COMPILE TIME; the artifact carries 1u64 << 63 as a baked value. A theorem about this module is a theorem about a computation that PRODUCED part of the artifact, not about one the artifact performs.
link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.same_registry_writer: record_green -- the sole writer, on DerivedAgreed, for BOTH seams
link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.same_markers_gate: flip_registry.rs:641 -- emit_lifetime_markers() && !markers_exact, consulted identically on both seams
link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.why_panic_arms_flip_at_CTFE_and_not_at_C: A POPULATION difference, not a gate difference, and this was measured rather than assumed. record_green is the sole registry writer for both seams and consults markers_exact identically. Of the 39 agreed assert-carrying bodies, 23 have markers_exact true and they are ALL const initializers -- vacuously, over two empty marker sequences. The 16 that are not are the runtime bodies, whose marker plans are refused by to_mir.rs:3202/:3780 (the func.scopes firewall) or by operands_of. So the asymmetry is: const initializers pass the marker gate for free, and the four runtime assert-carrying candidates do not pass it at all.

one_axis_where_it_is_STRONGER.what: verify_assert_parity (flip.rs:1767) verified 1 assert; on all 178 codegen flips that check is vacuous at 0
one_axis_where_it_is_STRONGER.detail: Both seams run verify_assert_parity, which walks the derived and built bodies in canonical DFS preorder and requires the assert sequences to match in COUNT, KIND CLASS (AssertClass::Overflow(BinOp) / DivByZero / RemByZero) and POLARITY. asserts=N in the event is the number VERIFIED. Every codegen flip in this crate reports asserts=0, so for all nine earlier chains that check establishes nothing; here it establishes one Overflow-class assert.

link_2b_on_the_ctfe_seam.the_honest_summary: More producer-side checking on the assert axis, and less artifact-shaped binding on the instruction axis. Neither sentence substitutes for the other, and this chain is not claimed to have link 2b in the codegen sense.

build_items.why_not: IRInst.assert : Nat -> IRInst has been a constructor since eval_ir_syntax was written, and ir_exec has always had the case IRInst.assert c => ir_assert_exec s (ir_getd s c). ir_assert_exec is not a stub: it reads the scrutinee through ir_as_bool, faults type_error not_bool on anything that is not a Bool, and hands a decided Bool to ir_assert_b, whose false minor is IRConfig.halted (IROutcome.ub IRFault.assert_failed) and whose true minor is ir_advance.

semantics_build_item.what: IRCastOp.bitcast, which was a blanket ir_width_fault
semantics_build_item.why_the_old_refusal_did_not_cover_this: Its stated reason -- a cell-addressed model has no representation to reinterpret -- is still right for the cases it was written about. It does not cover the only bitcast the shipped kernel emits: i32 -> u32, two INTEGER types at the SAME width, where IRScalar.int_ n already IS the canonical width-w bit pattern (that is what makes ir_sext_value and ir_wrap mean anything) and nothing is reinterpreted.
semantics_build_item.what_was_added: ir_bitcast_int / ir_bitcast_eval in eval_ir_ops, plus four kernel-executed theorems
what_stays_refused: a WIDTH MISMATCH (ir_nat_eqb sw dw) -- ir_bitcast_width_mismatch_fails_closed, for every scalar
a FLOAT on either side -- ir_ty_int_width declines IRTy.float_, so bitcast f64 -> u64 is refused AT THE SAME WIDTH (ir_bitcast_float_still_refused)
a POINTER or aggregate on either side, for the same reason
IRCastOp.transmute entirely -- a different constructor, so transmute::<f64, u64>, the counterexample the original refusal names, is untouched (ir_transmute_still_refused)
semantics_build_item.new_trust_added: none -- ir_wrap, ir_nat_eqb, ir_ty_int_width and ir_int1 were all already relied on by the integer arithmetic lane

candidate_selection.source: docs/analysis/frontier-2026-08-16.md §2 -- '"Panic arms 0" is a statement about CODEGEN flips only. 21 of the 32 CTFE flips carry an Inst::Assert'
candidate_selection.note: Re-derived by a parser written for this job over this lane's own whole-crate dump, joining flip events to coverage rows on def_index and IR bodies to coverage rows on func_id (7,571 of 7,571 bodyful fn bodies, 0 join defects). The assert count comes from the event's own asserts= field, which is the number verify_assert_parity VERIFIED.

no_overflow.shape: %2, %3 = mul.overflow usize %0, %1 ; %6 = select bool %3, false, true ; assert %6 ; ret %2
no_overflow.refused_because: every operand is `usize`, which the CFG type lane deliberately leaves as the loud `?usize` rather than deciding the target's pointer width, and assert_lanes refuses an unresolved type on EITHER side. Chaining one would mean assuming a width. The ninth chain established that refusal for its two unchained zext siblings and this lane inherits it rather than reopening it.
no_overflow.what_a_later_lane_would_also_owe: IRInst.overflow, which is one of exactly TWO arms of the 28-arm dispatch that are the tagged unmodelled outcome, plus a multi-result binder. The syntax already has IROverflowOp at 3/3 and IRNode already carries a result LIST, so the missing pieces are an evaluator and a binder -- and, first, a decision about usize.

shift_in_range.shape: %0 = const u64 1 ; %1 = const i32 K ; %2 = bitcast i32 %1 to u32 ; %3 = const u32 64 ; %4 = icmp ult u32 %2, %3 ; assert %4 ; %5 = sext i32 %1 to u64 ; %6 = shl u64 %0, %5 ; ret %6
shift_in_range.note: 127 is TWO_POW_127 and is u128 rather than u64.

candidate_selection.chosen_on: CONTENT: the shift amount 63 is exactly ONE BELOW the assert's own boundary, so the failing side is ADJACENT and the boundary can be pinned from both sides by execution -- ir_mt_exact returns a value at 63 and ir_mt_oob_traps panics at 64. It is also unique among the twelve rather than one of a duplicated pair (seven of the twelve share a shift amount with another), and it is load-bearing in the kernel: META_TAG is the metavariable tag bit of the type checker's local context and push_low_local's own printed contract quotes it (ENSURES: result.as_u64() < (1u64 << 63)).

cost.harness: cargo test -p clean-verify --test evalir_scratchpad (the EvalIr bundle, not the full spec)
cost.note: The expensive declaration is the nine-step Eq.refl. Three different spellings of the right-hand side -- the readable reflected constant, a near-exact residual and the EXACT residual in the machine's own vocabulary -- all cost the same ~360 s, so the cost is the run and the residue fold rather than a mis-spelled RHS. The ANSWER is never computed: ir_nat_mul recurses on its second argument, so normalizing ir_nat_mul 1 (ir_nat_pow2 63) would cost 2^63 Nat.rec unfoldings, and it stays an unreduced application on both sides. The counterfactual at shift 64 halts at step 6 and costs 0.045 s, which is the measurement that localizes the cost to the last three steps.

superseded_at_head.emitted_body_note: The emitted body is instruction-for-instruction identical to the text pinned in meta_tag_shl.trust-ir.txt; instr_count is unchanged at 9 and the body contains no `gep`. Only whole-crate NUMBERING moved (functy-index), which renumbers on any clean-kernel or producer change and which the semantics provably does not consult: ir_ty_is_agg_enum_any / ir_ty_is_agg_struct_any (spec/core_spec/eval_ir_ops.rs) prove ir_ty_is_agg is Bool.true at EVERY id, and ir_const_agg_eval reaches the type only through it. The .trust-ir.txt fixture is therefore NOT refreshed -- refreshing all eleven was TRIED and measured, and it turns crystal_a1_lineage from 59/59 to 57 passed / 2 failed: expr_path_step_clone's const-type lane (emitted enum176 vs the registered ir_ep_tstep := IRTy.enum_ 181) and level_is_zero.rs:77's hard-coded assert!(body.contains("call @func.4914")).
superseded_at_head.this_fixture_is_not_overwritten: Every measured field ABOVE remains a correct, internally consistent record of the build it was taken at, and is deliberately left alone. It is NOT a claim about HEAD. The 2026-08-19 revalidation is recorded in the file named above: one sealed driver (guard PASS before every run, positive behavioural identification against a pre-wave-DZ control), one recipe (scripts/trust_ir_build.sh --print-only), reproduced over three clean non-incremental builds with byte-identical coverage.json and trust-ir.txt, with a negative control at 0 flip events crate-wide.
superseded_at_head.why_it_is_not_re_pinned_in_place: A partial re-pin would manufacture a fixture that describes no single build. The `build` block here was measured on a DIFFERENT recipe -- RUSTFLAGS applied the flip crate-wide, which is why it records flip_events_all_from_clean_kernel: false over thousands of events -- while scripts/trust_ir_build.sh attaches -Ztrust-ir-flip to the SUBJECT UNIT ALONE, so foreign events are 0 by construction and the two `build` blocks are not comparable field by field. Moving `lineage` while leaving them is exactly the mixing that level_kind_ord.lineage.json's `measurement_scope` warns against.
